Boundary conditions at the anchor pixels

Source: R/metric-anchors.R
ef_anchor_conditions.Rd

Completes an anchor set (ef_select_anchors() or ef_anchors()) with the boundary conditions of the METRIC calibration (stage [B] of dev/specs/anchor-pixels.md section 1.3, decision D-AP-03): at each anchor pixel, the target latent heat flux \(LE\) and the target sensible heat flux \(H = R_n - G - LE\), from the net radiation, the soil heat flux and the instantaneous reference evapotranspiration at that pixel; then one calibration point per class, which is what the sensible heat calibration consumes.

Usage

ef_anchor_conditions(
  anchors,
  rn,
  g,
  etr_inst,
  lambda,
  etrf_cold,
  etrf_hot = NULL,
  le_hot = NULL,
  reference,
  source,
  status,
  etr_source = NULL,
  zom = NULL,
  u_blend = NULL,
  pressure = NULL
)

Arguments

anchors

An earthflux_anchors object.

rn

Numeric vector or matrix on the grid of the anchors. Net radiation [W m-2] (e.g. ef_net_radiation()). Finite where not missing; must not be missing at an anchor pixel.

g

Numeric vector or matrix on the same grid. Soil heat flux [W m-2]. Same conditions as rn.

etr_inst

Numeric. Instantaneous reference evapotranspiration [mm h-1], > 0: a single value for the scene (one station) or a layer on the grid (e.g. a regionalised surface), evaluated at the overpass time of each pixel. Its value at each anchor pixel is used.

lambda

Numeric. Latent heat of vaporization [J kg-1] from ef_lambda(), a single value or a layer on the grid. The same lambda (same method) must be used in the conversion of LE to ET (decision P0-7). Checked to lie in [1e6, 1e7] (unit guard).

etrf_cold

Numeric. Reference ET fraction imposed at the cold anchor, the coefficient \(k\) of \(ET_{cold} = k \cdot ET_{r,inst}\) [-]; finite and > 0. No default (decision D-AP-04).

etrf_hot, le_hot

Numeric. Condition of the hot anchor; give exactly one: the reference ET fraction at the hot anchor (etrf_hot, finite and >= 0; 0 for dry bare soil) or its latent heat flux (le_hot [W m-2], finite and >= 0). No default (decision D-AP-05).

reference

Character. Reference surface of etr_inst: "alfalfa" (ETr) or "grass" (ETo). Must be the reference of the daily extrapolation (checked by the orchestration).

source

Character. Source of etrf_cold and of the hot condition.

status

Character. Their verification status: "TODO", "CANDIDATA" or "VERIFICADA".

etr_source

Character or NULL. Origin of etr_inst (e.g. "station", "gwr"), recorded.

zom, u_blend, pressure

Numeric or NULL. Optional inputs of the sensible heat calibration passed through to the calibration points, so that ef_calibrate_h() can read the anchor object directly: momentum roughness length [m] (> 0, e.g. from ef_zom() on the grid), wind speed at the blending height [m s-1] (>= 0) and atmospheric pressure [kPa] (> 0, e.g. ef_air_pressure()). Each is a single value or a layer on the grid; its value at each anchor pixel is aggregated with the aggregate of the anchor set. Not used in the boundary conditions.

Value

The earthflux_anchors object with:

  • calibration_points completed with the columns rn, g [W m-2], etr_inst [mm h-1], lambda [J kg-1], etrf [-], le_target and h_target [W m-2], with h_target = rn - g - le_target exactly in each row, followed by zom [m], u_blend [m s-1] and pressure [kPa] when given. With them, calibration_points has every column required by the sensible heat calibration (type, lst, elevation, zom, rn, g, le_target, u_blend, pressure; anchor_id optional), one row per class;

  • conditions: a list with pixels (per anchor pixel: id, type, cell, utc_hour, rn, g, etr_inst, lambda, etrf, le_target, h_target), etrf_cold, hot_condition ("etrf" or "le"), etrf_hot, le_hot, reference, etr_source, etr_inst_layer and lambda_layer (whether a layer was used), source, status and equations;

  • dispersion completed with the new variables;

  • flags completed with EF_ANCHOR_COLD_H_NEGATIVE (record scope: rows of pixels of the cold class with \(H < 0\)) and EF_ANCHOR_HOT_LE_ASSUMED_ZERO (object scope: the hot LE is 0 by assumption, not from a soil water balance).

Details

At each anchor pixel \(i\): $$ET_i = ETrF_i \cdot ET_{r,inst,i}$$ $$LE_i = \frac{ET_i \, \lambda_i \, \rho_w}{3600 \times 1000}$$ $$H_i = R_{n,i} - G_i - LE_i$$ with \(ETrF_i\) = etrf_cold for cold pixels and etrf_hot for hot pixels (or \(LE_i\) = le_hot), \(\rho_w\) = 1000 kg m-3, 3600 s h-1 and 1000 mm m-1. The calibration point of each class aggregates rn, g, etr_inst, lambda and le_target with the aggregate of the anchor set and sets h_target = rn - g - le_target (for "mean" this equals the mean of the per-pixel targets). etrf of the hot point is derived from le_target when le_hot is given.

Assumptions (CANDIDATA): the cold anchor is fully covered, well watered agricultural vegetation evaporating at etrf_cold times the reference; the hot anchor is dry agricultural bare soil; etr_inst is representative of each anchor location and overpass time; no lateral heat transport. A negative \(H\) at the cold anchor is not an error (advection) but it is flagged.

Errors: a missing rn, g, etr_inst or lambda at an anchor pixel raises earthflux_anchor_na_input (fields variable, index = rows of pixels); invalid or out-of-domain arguments raise earthflux_input_error / earthflux_domain_error; etr_inst <= 0 raises earthflux_domain_error.

Verification status: the forms are VERIFICADA (SEBAL-Idaho 2002): Waters et al. (2002), p. 30, step 5a (cold anchor: \(H_{cold} = R_n - G - 1.05\,\lambda ET_r\), ETr being the alfalfa reference at the image time, pp. 13 and 38) and p. 31, step 5b (hot anchor: \(H_{hot} = R_n - G - \lambda ET_{hot}\) with \(ET_{hot} = 0\) for a dry bare agricultural field, or from a soil water balance after rain in the previous 1-4 days). The values 1.05 and 0 are the ones of the manual (also "generally" in appendix 8, p. 81), but they stay explicit arguments without default (decisions D-AP-04 and D-AP-05, P0-8: no coefficient by default in the anchor core). The unit conversion is VERIFICADA (FAO-56, box 8, with 3600 s h-1; Eq. 42 of the manual). The cross-check with Allen et al. (2007) remains desirable but is no longer blocking.

References

Allen, R. G., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2007). Satellite-based energy balance for mapping evapotranspiration with internalized calibration (METRIC) - Model. Journal of Irrigation and Drainage Engineering, 133(4), 380-394. doi:10.1061/(ASCE)0733-9437(2007)133:4(380)

Waters, R., Allen, R., Bastiaanssen, W., Tasumi, M., & Trezza, R. (2002). SEBAL: Surface Energy Balance Algorithms for Land. Idaho implementation. Advanced training and users manual (Version 1.0). University of Idaho and Idaho Department of Water Resources.

Allen, R. G., Pereira, L. S., Raes, D., & Smith, M. (1998). Crop evapotranspiration: Guidelines for computing crop water requirements (FAO Irrigation and Drainage Paper 56). FAO, Rome. ISBN 92-5-104219-5.

See also

Other anchor pixel functions: ef_anchor_criteria(), ef_anchor_pick(), ef_anchor_rule(), ef_anchors(), ef_homogeneity(), ef_select_anchors()

Examples

lst <- c(300, 321, 310)
anchors <- ef_anchors(cold = 1, hot = 2, lst = lst,
                      ndvi = c(0.85, 0.10, 0.4),
                      albedo = c(0.20, 0.25, 0.2), aggregate = "none")
# Coefficients of the SEBAL Idaho manual, passed explicitly (no defaults)
anchors <- ef_anchor_conditions(
  anchors, rn = c(700, 500, 600), g = c(100, 120, 110), etr_inst = 0.8,
  lambda = ef_lambda(method = "constant"), etrf_cold = 1.05,
  etrf_hot = 0, reference = "alfalfa",
  source = "Waters et al. (2002), SEBAL Idaho manual, pp. 30-31",
  status = "VERIFICADA", etr_source = "station"
)
anchors$calibration_points[, c("type", "lst", "rn", "g", "le_target",
                               "h_target")]
#>   type lst  rn   g le_target  h_target
#> 1 cold 300 700 100  571.6667  28.33333
#> 2  hot 321 500 120    0.0000 380.00000
